pages.c16-p01: Explain what generative AI is and give examples of what it can create
pages.c16-p02: Describe how a large language model writes by predicting the next word
pages.c16-p03: Write clear prompts and improve them step by step to get better results
pages.c16-p04: Explain why generative AI makes mistakes and shows bias, and check its output
pages.c16-p05: Use generative AI honestly in schoolwork and respect copyright and ownership
pages.c16-p06: Discuss the impact of generative AI on jobs, the environment and society, and form a reasoned opinion

q.q: What is generative AI?
o: AI that creates new content such as text or images
q.why: Generative AI makes new content.

q.q: Which of these is NOT an example of generative AI?
o: An app that makes a picture from a description
q.why: A spam filter sorts; it doesn't create.

q.q: What does an AI model learn from?
q.why: Models learn patterns from training data.

q.q: Which best describes a trained AI model?
o: A large set of numbers that captures patterns
q.why: The model is the learned set of numbers.

q.q: What is a prompt?
o: The data used to train the AI
The instruction you give a generative AI tool
q.why: You control generative AI with prompts.

q.q: Why might you get a different answer if you ask a chatbot the same question twice?
o: It chooses from many likely options each time
q.why: Generation involves choosing among likely options.

q.q: Which type of content can generative AI create?
o: Text, images, audio, video and code
q.why: Generators exist for all these kinds of content.

q.q: Face unlock on a phone is an example of AI that...
q.why: Face unlock recognises you; it doesn't create.

q.q: Which statement about training data is true?
o: It is usually a huge collection of examples
It is typed in by the user each time
q.why: Models need very large datasets.

q.q: Learning to draw a dog after seeing thousands of dogs is similar to how an AI model...
q.why: Models learn general patterns from many examples.

q.q: What does LLM stand for?
q.why: LLM = large language model.

q.q: What powers most modern chatbots?
q.why: Chatbots use LLMs.

q.q: How does an LLM write an answer?
o: By copying a whole answer from a book
By looking it up in a dictionary
By predicting the next token over and over
q.why: LLMs generate one predicted token at a time.

q.q: What is a token?
o: A word or part of a word
q.why: Tokens are chunks of text.

q.q: The word "unbelievable" might be split into tokens like...
q.why: Long words are often split into pieces.

q.q: When predicting the next token, an LLM gives each possible token a...
q.why: It scores how likely each token is.

q.q: Why can a chatbot sound confident but be wrong?
o: It predicts likely words rather than checking facts
q.why: Fluency comes from patterns, not fact-checking.

q.q: An LLM was trained mainly on...
q.why: Language models learn from text.

q.q: What happens when an LLM picks a less likely next word?
o: The text becomes more varied or surprising
q.why: Less likely choices add variety but risk nonsense.

q.q: Which of these is a sensible way to treat chatbot answers?
o: As a replacement for all teachers
Like a well-read friend who sometimes makes things up
q.why: Useful, but check what matters.

q.q: What is prompt engineering?
o: The skill of writing prompts that get useful results
q.why: Prompt engineering is crafting good prompts.

q.q: Which prompt is likely to give the most useful result?
o: Explain the water cycle to a 12-year-old in 4 numbered steps
q.why: Specific prompts remove the guesswork.

q.q: In a prompt, "You are a friendly science teacher" is an example of a...
q.why: Giving the AI a role sets its voice and level.

q.q: In a prompt, "in five bullet points" is an example of...
q.why: Format tells the AI how to lay it out.

q.q: In a prompt, "under 100 words" is an example of a...
q.why: Limits set boundaries such as length.

q.q: Adding "for a Year 9 revision page" to a prompt gives the AI...
q.why: Context is background the AI needs.

q.q: What is iteration when using AI?
o: Asking once and accepting the answer
q.why: Iteration improves results step by step.

q.q: Which follow-up is a good way to refine an answer?
o: Make point 3 simpler and give a real example
q.why: Specific follow-ups improve answers.

q.q: Why should you not put your home address into an AI tool?
o: What you type may be stored and used
q.why: Prompts can be kept and used by the company.

q.q: Which of these is safe to include in a prompt?
o: A photo of your friend without permission
q.why: Never share personal information or other people's images.

q.q: What is an AI hallucination?
o: When AI states something false as if it were true
When AI shows a picture of a dream
q.why: Hallucinations are confident false outputs.

q.q: Which of these could be a hallucination?
o: A made-up quote from a famous scientist
q.why: AI can invent quotes and sources.

q.q: Why do AI hallucinations happen?
o: The model predicts likely words, not checked facts
q.why: Prediction isn't the same as checking.

q.q: What is bias in AI?
o: Treating some people or ideas unfairly or one-sidedly
q.why: Bias is unfairness in outputs.

q.q: Where does AI bias usually come from?
o: Patterns and stereotypes in its training data
q.why: Biased data creates biased models.

q.q: An image generator asked for "a CEO" draws mostly men. This is an example of...
q.why: It reflects a stereotype from its data.

q.q: What does "verify" mean?
q.why: Verifying means checking.

q.q: What is the best way to check a fact an AI gave you?
o: Compare it with two reliable sources
Ask someone who agrees with you
q.why: Cross-check with reliable sources.

q.q: Which source is most reliable for checking a science fact?
o: An anonymous comment on a video
q.why: Reputable, checked sources are best.

q.q: An AI gives you a web link as a source. What should you do?
o: Open it and check it says what the AI claims
q.why: AI can invent links.

q.q: Why should you take extra care with AI statements about real people?
o: It is always illegal to search for people
False information can hurt real people
AI is never wrong about people
q.why: Mistakes about real people can be harmful.

q.q: Which question helps you spot bias in an answer?
q.why: Looking for missing views helps spot bias.

q.q: What is plagiarism?
o: Presenting someone else's work as your own
q.why: Passing off others' work, including AI work.

q.q: Handing in an essay written by AI as your own is...
q.why: It's not your own work.

q.q: Which is an honest way to use AI for homework (if allowed)?
o: Copying its answer word for word
Getting it to write the homework
Using it secretly in a test
Asking it to quiz you on the topic
q.why: Quizzing helps you learn.

q.q: What might happen if you use AI in GCSE coursework when it isn't allowed?
o: You could lose marks or the qualification
q.why: It can count as malpractice.

q.q: What should an acknowledgement of AI use include?
o: The tool, date, what you asked and how you used it
q.why: A clear statement of how AI was used.

q.q: What is copyright?
o: The legal right protecting creative work from being copied without permission
q.why: Copyright protects creators.

q.q: Why do many artists object to generative AI?
o: Their work was used for training without permission or payment
q.why: Consent and payment for training data are big issues.

q.q: Who decides the rules about AI and copyright?
o: Courts and governments, and the rules are still developing
q.why: The law is still being worked out.

q.q: Which of these follows school rules best?
o: Saying which AI tool you used and how
q.why: Being open about AI use is honest.

q.q: Using AI to get feedback on a paragraph you wrote is usually...
o: helpful, if your teacher allows it
q.why: You still do the writing yourself.

q.q: What is automation?
o: Machines or software doing tasks people used to do
q.why: Automation replaces human tasks.

q.q: Which task is generative AI likely to automate?
o: Refereeing a football match in person
q.why: Routine writing is easy to automate.

q.q: Which new job has been created by AI?
q.why: New AI-related roles are appearing.

q.q: Which human skill becomes more valuable as AI improves?
q.why: Judgement and critical thinking matter more.

q.q: Where do large AI models run?
q.why: Big models run on servers in data centres.

q.q: Why do data centres use lots of water?
q.why: Cooling servers needs water.

q.q: What is regulation?
q.why: Regulation means rules, often laws.

q.q: What is the EU AI Act?
o: A set of rules that sorts AI systems by risk
q.why: It regulates AI by risk level.

q.q: Which is an opportunity of generative AI?
o: Helping people learn in new ways
q.why: Personalised learning is a benefit.

q.q: Which is a risk of generative AI?
q.why: Realistic fakes can spread misinformation.

q.q: Which statement about AI and jobs is most accurate?
o: Every job will vanish next year
Many jobs will change as people work alongside AI
AI will never affect any job
q.why: Change is more common than total loss.

q.q: Why might relying on AI too much be a problem?
o: You might lose skills you never practise
q.why: Over-reliance can weaken skills.

q.q: What is one way to use AI more responsibly for the environment?
o: Run it all day in the background
Use it when it's genuinely useful, not endlessly for fun
Ask the same question hundreds of times
q.why: Every prompt uses energy.

q.q: Which group is a chatbot NOT able to replace?
o: People who check and judge its work
q.why: Human oversight is still needed.

q.q: What is the main difference between a search engine and a chatbot?
o: A search engine finds existing pages; a chatbot generates new text
q.why: Chatbots generate; search engines retrieve.

q.q: Which is the most important reason to know how LLMs work?
o: So you know when to trust and when to check their answers
q.why: Understanding helps you use them wisely.

q.q: What does "temperature" control in some chatbots?
o: How varied or surprising the answers are
q.why: Higher temperature means more random choices.

q.q: A chatbot gives a reference to a book that doesn't exist. This is a...
q.why: Invented sources are hallucinations.

q.q: What is the risk of using an AI answer in homework without checking it?
o: It may contain errors you hand in as fact
It will be in another language
q.why: Unchecked errors become your errors.

q.q: Which is the best prompt for a revision quiz?
o: Make 5 multiple-choice questions on the water cycle for Year 8, answers at the end
q.why: Detail gets a useful result.

q.q: You get a long, confusing answer. What is the best next step?
o: Refine the prompt, e.g. "explain in 3 short bullet points"
q.why: Refining improves results.

q.q: Which of these is personal information?
o: Your full name and home address
The year group you're writing for
q.why: Personal information identifies you.

q.q: Which helps reduce bias in AI systems?
o: Training on fairer, more varied data and testing for bias
q.why: Better data and testing reduce bias.

q.q: An AI says "Lough Erne is the largest lake in the world". What should you do?
o: Check a reliable source: it's false
Believe it because it sounds local
q.why: Lough Erne is not the world's largest lake: always verify.

q.q: Why might a school only allow certain AI tools?
o: They have checked them for safety and privacy
q.why: Schools approve tools that protect pupils' data.

q.q: Which part of the prompt "You are a coach. Give me a 10-minute warm-up for netball, as a numbered list" is the task?
o: Give me a 10-minute warm-up for netball
q.why: The task is what you want it to do.

q.q: Generative AI is a type of...
q.why: It is one branch of AI.

q.q: What do generative AI models need huge amounts of computing power for?
q.why: Training is very computer-intensive.

q.q: What is the best description of how generative AI "knows" things?
o: It looks up every answer live
It understands everything like a human
It has learned patterns from data, not facts it truly understands
q.why: It works from learned patterns.

q.q: Which is an example of AI-generated code?
o: A program written by an AI assistant from a description
A spreadsheet you made by hand
q.why: AI can generate code from descriptions.

q.q: What does it mean that AI tools may "use your prompts to improve their models"?
o: Your prompts make the AI slower
What you type might be used as training data
q.why: Your inputs may become training data.

q.q: Which statement about the UK's approach to AI regulation is true?
o: Existing regulators apply principles like safety and fairness in their own areas
AI is completely banned in the UK
There are no rules at all
q.why: The UK asks existing regulators to apply AI principles.

q.q: Which is a fair reason someone might support generative AI in schools?
o: It means pupils never need to think
It can give quick, personal feedback to help pupils learn
q.why: Personal feedback is a genuine benefit.

q.q: Which is a fair reason someone might worry about generative AI in schools?
o: Pupils might hand in work that isn't their own
It helps translate for new pupils
q.why: Academic honesty is a genuine concern.

q.q: What is the purpose of the "Context" part of a prompt recipe?
o: Give background the AI needs to tailor its answer
q.why: Context tailors the answer.

q.q: An LLM is asked "2 + 2 =". Why does it usually answer "4"?
o: That pattern appeared extremely often in its training data
It has a built-in calculator for all sums
q.why: Very common patterns are predicted reliably.

q.q: Which of these is the best summary of generative AI?
o: Powerful and useful, but it can be wrong, biased or misused
q.why: A balanced view is most accurate.

q.q: Which of these is an example of an AI image generator being used?
o: Taking a photo with your phone camera
Typing "a lighthouse at sunset, watercolour style" and getting a new picture
q.why: The picture is created from a text prompt.

q.q: Which describes a chatbot?
o: A program you can hold a conversation with
q.why: Chatbots respond conversationally.

q.q: Why does a chatbot not need to store every sentence it was trained on?
o: It has learned patterns it can use to write new sentences
q.why: Models learn patterns rather than storing copies.

q.q: Which prompt gives the AI the best context?
o: Explain fractions to a Year 8 pupil who finds them hard, using pizza examples
q.why: Audience and examples are useful context.

q.q: You asked an AI for a 100-word summary and got 400 words. What should you do?
o: Ask the same thing again exactly
q.why: A specific follow-up refines the answer.

q.q: A chatbot quotes a statistic with no source. What is the sensible response?
o: Use it in your homework straight away
Assume it is correct because it is a number
Treat it as unverified until you find it in a reliable source
q.why: Unsourced numbers may be hallucinated.

q.q: Which of these makes bias in an AI system MORE likely?
o: Testing the model with many different users
Training data that mostly shows one group of people
q.why: Unbalanced data leads to biased output.

q.q: When is it fine to use AI for school work?
o: Whenever you want, without telling anyone
When your teacher allows it and you say how you used it
q.why: Follow the rules and be open.

q.q: An AI image copies the style of a living artist and is sold as if they made it. What is the main problem?
o: It took too long to make
It is dishonest and may break copyright
q.why: Passing it off as the artist's work is deceptive.

q.q: Which of these is a reason AI regulation is needed?
o: To reduce harms such as unfair decisions and misinformation
q.why: Rules aim to reduce real harms.

q.q: What is an AI safety tester's job?
o: Checking AI models for dangerous or harmful behaviour before release
q.why: Testers look for risks before models are released.
